speakers.name: Chao Jia
speakers.bio: Chao Jia, Vice President of Technology at ModelBest and Co-founder of the OpenBMB open-source community. He is primarily responsible for organizing the R&D and open-source management of the MiniCPM series of on-device models. Dubbed the "ModelBest's Little Steel Cannon" the MiniCPM family—which includes the MiniCPM large language model and the MiniCPM-o omni-modal model—has earned widespread acclaim in the global AI community for its high efficiency, low cost, and ability to "punch above its weight." To date, these projects have amassed over 30,000 stars on GitHub and exceeded 24 million downloads worldwide, establishing themselves as benchmark works in the field of on-device AI.

speakers.name: Charbel Dandjinou
speakers.bio: Charbel is the founder and CTO of Reflexion Robotics, a Paris-based startup building A OS  - a safety runtime for embodied AI. Previously AI Research Engineer and MLOps Tech Lead at EXXACT Robotics. He also founded IROKO and the Deep Takka research lab, focused on making AI accessible and inclusive.
speakers.roleOrg: CTO - Founder - AI research engineer, Reflexion Robotics

speakers.name: Crozet Sébastien
speakers.bio: Sébastien Crozet has been in love with the Rust programming language since its earliest days. He is the creator and maintainer of popular open-source libraries, including nalgebra and Rapier, for the Rust ecosystem that specialize in linear algebra, geometry, and physics. He is the founder of Dimforge where he focuses on contributing to the future of cross-platform scientific computing and AI.

speakers.bio: 2008-2017微软 技术leader 从事微软Azure企业云Dynamics365平台研发工作 2017- 华为技术有限公司 技术专家/产品总监 从事研发工具链，编程语言，IDE等核心基础软件研发工作。 在华为公司工作期间，先后作为首席技术专家和项目经理从事华为移动端AI研发工具，公司级AI研发平台，华为昇腾AI芯片工具链，鸿蒙OS工具链等相关工作。 2021年起负责华为编程语言和IDE基础软件的研发业务，并担任项目群总监，从事自主可控的编程语言及IDE开发工具的核心技术研发工作，对国产应用编程语言的技术规划，产品化，产业落地进展等工作出了重要的贡献

speakers.name: Ervin Xie
speakers.bio: Weiyu Xie is a fifth-year Ph.D. student in the Institute for High Performance Computing, Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University. His research interests include computer systems, large language model (LLM) inference, graph computing, and databases.

speakers.name: guillaume blaquiere
speakers.bio:
Guillaume is a Google Developer Expert on Cloud Platform since 2019 and works at Carrefour as Group Data Architect. 

Initially Java developer, and despite positions of responsibilities, he has always kept his wish to create, develop, discover and test new solutions, especially in the Cloud, the AI & genAI. He notably contributed to Python and Go open source project and libraries (Google SDK, Airflow, ADK). 

Innovation addict and Google Cloud 3x certified, writer and speaker in his free time, he's fascinated by the serverless and genAI solution and all the "usual" problems that they solve.

speakers.name: Jigyasa Grover (co-speaker Rishabh Misra)
speakers.bio:
12-time award-winning AI lead and 'Sculpting Data For ML' author Jigyasa Grover drives rider personalization innovation at Uber after transforming Twitter/X, Facebook/Meta, Faire, and Bordo AI with large-scale ML systems. Handpicked by Google for their I/O keynote, she serves on Google's Developer Advisory Board while advising social search engine Diem and other Silicon Valley startups. 

As a LinkedIn Learning instructor, Jigyasa educates thousands of professionals worldwide on cutting-edge AI-powered applications and agentic AI systems, solidifying her status as a thought leader in artificial intelligence education. As a Google Developer Expert, Women Techmaker Ambassador, and World Economic Forum Global Shaper, Jigyasa has also been featured in Forbes, Business Insider, VentureBeat, and International Business Times, and has elevated panels with Harvard University, Preston-Werner Ventures, Norwegian Business School, Humanitarian Frontier in AI, Women in Data, and more to her name. 

The UC San Diego alumna has secured funding from the Canadian and Norwegian governments, the Linux Foundation, and multiple tech giants, enabling work that transcends geographical boundaries. With 200+ media features and contributions to open source recognized by Apache and Python Software Foundations, she mentors next-generation talent while shaping AI's future through advisory roles at Bezoku AI, Las Positas College, and various AI forums.
speakers.role: ML Tech Lead • 12x AI + Open Source Award Winner • Google Developer Advisory Board Member • LinkedIn [in]structor • Book Author • Startup Advisor / Speaker / Tech Creator • Featured @ Forbes, UN, Google I/O, and more!
speakers.roleOrg: ML Tech Lead • 12x AI + Open Source Award Winner • Google Developer Advisory Board Member • LinkedIn [in]structor • Book Author • Startup Advisor / Speaker / Tech Creator • Featured @ Forbes, UN, Google I/O, and more!, Uber

speakers.name: Luke Lu
speakers.bio: Luke is a student at the University of Texas at Austin and the founder of Correx, an open-source robotic task verification and safety compliance layer. His journey in robotics began as a competitor, rising through the ranks of competitive robotics to claim a world championship title. That experience ignited a drive to mentor aspiring engineers and contribute to the open-source robotics community. Today, Luke channels that same competitive energy into founding technology ventures at the intersection of AI and robotics, believing that the best ideas should be accessible to everyone willing to build them.

speakers.name: Marcin Zubrzycki
speakers.bio: I'm a SWE @ StrongDM (now part of Delinea), I'm currently studying Algorithmic Computer Science @ WrocTech - currently studying Algorithmic Computer Science at Wrocław University of Science and Technology.
speakers.roleOrg: Software Engineer, StrongDM (now part of Delinea)

speakers.name: Markus Tavenrath
speakers.bio:
Markus Tavenrath studied computer science with a focus on computer graphics at RWTH Aachen University. This academic background provided a solid foundation for his career in the technology industry.

In 2008, Markus joined NVIDIA, where he began working on real-time ray tracing on GPUs. Over the years, he has contributed to performance optimization for ray tracing, scene graphs, OpenGL, WebGL, Vulkan, and AI. His work has played a role in advancing these technologies.

Markus is also a co-founder of the Vulkan-Hpp project, which has been beneficial to the Vulkan community. His efforts have helped improve the use and implementation of Vulkan.

Recently, Markus was elected as the Chair of the ML Council at Khronos. In this role, he helps coordinate and support AI and machine learning initiatives within the Khronos group. His election to this position reflects his expertise and leadership qualities.

Markus Tavenrath is a dedicated professional whose contributions have positively impacted the technological landscape at NVIDIA and beyond.

speakers.name: Merel Theisen
speakers.bio: I am a Principal Software Engineer at QuantumBlack, where I am currently the tech lead of Kedro, an open-source project part of the Linux Foundation. I have over ten years of experience in the software industry, with most of my career focused on backend product engineering. I am passionate about building products that solve real user problems, and I care deeply about creating robust, well-tested software that follows good engineering principles. I am also a strong advocate for open-source software, and I find working with the community to be both inspiring and energising.

speakers.name: Minako Kojima
speakers.bio: I'm the Head of Developer Relations at Kimi, where I've also held positions in post-training and infrastructure. Prior to joining Kimi, I worked as an algorithm engineer at Google. I won several gold medals at ACM ICPC regional contests during college.
speakers.roleOrg: Head of Developer Relations, Moonshot AI

speakers.name: Nouamane Tazi
speakers.bio: Nouamane Tazi is a Machine Learning Research Engineer at Hugging Face, specializing in training large language models. He is a co-author of SmolLM3 and The Ultra Scale Playbook, and his research spans NLP, deep learning, and scalable AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: Ran Shemtov
speakers.bio: Ran is a web developer with over a decade of experience building products for the web. Since 2023, he has been deeply involved in the emerging world of AI-powered applications, helping companies design and bring AI agents into production. At CopilotKit, Ran works closely with teams building real-world AI experiences, guiding them through the challenges of turning LLM prototypes into systems that serve real users.

speakers.name: Rik Arends
speakers.bio: With 20+ years’ experience as a C/C++, JavaScript and more recently Rust developer, I've always been excited by using computation for visuals and audio. For this to work you need performance, and a smooth workflow enabled by the right tooling. After having everything I wanted with C except stable code I moved to JavaScript and web technologies. However, this never got to the point of being able to make fast applications that use modern CPU and GPU power. Now with Rust we have a new chance. I've been an entrepreneur my entire life building VJ software in the 00's, then web UI technology and web IDEs with Cloud9, and am now reimagining the developer workflow in Rust with Makepad. And lately how to leverage AI to write Rust and UI code.

speakers.name: Shiwei Liu
speakers.bio: Shiwei Liu is a group leader at Max Planck Institute for Intelligent System and a PI at ELLIS Institute Tubingen. He was a Royal Society Newton International Fellow at the University of Oxford. He previously served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Texas at Austin. He obtained his Ph.D. with Cum Laude from Eindhoven University of Technology in 2022. Dr. Liu has received two Rising Star Awards from KAUST and the Conference on Parsimony and Learning (CPAL). His Ph.D. thesis received the 2023 Best Dissertation Runner-up from Informatics Europe. He has a broad interests of life-cycle of large foundation models.
speakers.org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent System; ELLIS Institute Tübingen
speakers.roleOrg: Group Leader & PI, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent System; ELLIS Institute Tübingen

speakers.name: Vector Wang
speakers.bio: Gaotian (Vector) Wang is a Computer Science PhD student at Rice University. He is the creator of XLeRobot, a fully open-source, low-cost ($660) dual-arm mobile robot platform that has gained 4.8k+ GitHub stars and a global community of 6,000+ builders since its release in May 2025. XLeRobot is built on the Hugging Face LeRobot ecosystem and has been adopted by researchers, educators, and hobbyists worldwide.

His book series “Collegiate Programming Contests and Education” has been published in simplified and traditional Chinese and English: the former by respective publishers of mainland China and Taiwan, and the latter, the first book’s translation, by CRC Press. Since 2013, he has been giving lectures not only in China, but also in other countries.

speakers.name: Arturo Amor
speakers.bio:
I did my PhD in theoretical quantum physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), followed by a postdoctoral position in the same field at École Polytechnique in France. Since 2021, I have been a core contributor to scikit-learn, serving as a member of the documentation team to ensure clear, accessible and up-to-date documentation for easier usability.

Currently, I'm a co-founder at :probabl., a company founded by the scikit-learn creators and maintainers. In this role, I'm part of the training and certification team, where I work developing educational materials and certification programs that bridge the gap between theory and practice, helping professionals achieve internationally recognized standards in machine learning and the related good practices.

speakers.name: Eva Ma
speakers.bio: Taming the wild frontiers of generative AI. I design the structures that keep modern algorithms bounded, efficient, and aligned with human intent. Architecting the future of Atlas Cloud AI.

speakers.name: Junyi Zhong
speakers.bio: Dr. Junyi Zhong is a tech entrepreneur and AI researcher specializing in Trustworthy AI and blockchain systems. He is the CEO of INNAIO France, he focuses on AI-driven voice interfaces to advance information accessibility and global communication. He is also an active angel investor, supporting early-stage projects across AI and Web3.

speakers.name: Wei Wang（王伟）
speakers.bio: 王伟，奇点智能研究院开源技术委员会主任，工业和信息化部电子标准院开源治理标准总体组组长，联合国咨商开源创新专委会秘书长，华东师范大学教授，CCF杰出会员。牵头制定中国首套开源治理系列标准，研究聚焦开源治理与开源评价。在 ICSE、WWW、ACL 等顶会期刊发表论文百余篇，入选国家级创新人才项目、获国家级教学成果二等奖、上海开源创新卓越成果奖特等奖。

speakers.name: Wendy Seltzer
speakers.bio:
Wendy Seltzer is a lawyer and technologist, currently consulting via the Law Office of Wendy Seltzer. She is a founder of the First Person Cooperative, addressing governance of decentralized trust networks for personhood recognition and agency.

As Principal Identity Architect at Tucows, she helped to found the Ayra Association. She previously served as Strategy Lead and Counsel to the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) at MIT, improving the Web's security, availability, and interoperability through standards. As a Fellow with Harvard's Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society, Wendy founded the Lumen Project (formerly Chilling Effects Clearinghouse), the web's pioneering transparency report to measure the impact of legal takedown demands online. She seeks to improve technology policy in support of user-driven innovation and secure communication. She co-authored the second edition of Blown to Bits: Your Life, Liberty, and Happiness After the Digital Explosion.
speakers.roleOrg: Principal, Law Office of Wendy Seltzer

speakers.name: Xuan Huang (黄玄)
speakers.bio: Xuan Huang (@huxpro) is the Architect of Lynx at ByteDance, an open-source, cross-platform framework powering TikTok and CapCut. He is exploring what app frameworks should look like in the age of AI, and he was previously on the React Core Team at Meta.

speakers.name: Ziyan Wang
speakers.bio: A faculty member at a public university and the principal of a private business school, primarily engaged in education.

speakers.name: Rémi Louf
speakers.bio: Rémi is co-founder and CEO of .txt, building the infrastructure that makes agentic AI production-ready. His bet: the bottleneck isn't model intelligence; it's making AI output reliable, predictable, and composable at scale.

speakers.name: Drummond Reed
speakers.bio: Drummond has spent over a quarter-century in Internet identity, security, privacy, and trust infrastructure. He is currently founder of the First Person Project and a Director of the First Person Cooperative. He is co-author of the book, Self-Sovereign Identity (Manning Publications, 2021), and co-editor of the W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DID) 1.0 specification.

speakers.name: Michael Yuan
speakers.bio: Dr. Michael Yuan is a maintainer of WasmEdge Runtime (a CNCF project) and co-founder of Second State. He is the author of 5 books on software engineering published by Addison-Wesley, Prentice-Hall, and O'Reilly. Michael is a long-time open-source developer and has spoken at Open Source Summit, RustLab, GOSIM, and KubeCon.

speakers.name: Sir Timothy Gowers
speakers.bio: Sir Timothy Gowers is a Fields Medalist, Professor of Combinatorics at the Collège de France, and Research Professor at the University of Cambridge. His groundbreaking work applies analytic and combinatorial methods to number theory, and he has forged deep connections between combinatorics and functional analysis. He received the Fields Medal in 1998 and was knighted in 2012.

Hosts Follow the Rabbit, a podcast on cultural phenomena. Powered by his own agentic AI infrastructure.

speakers.bio: Head of AI at CODATA, working on Semantic Croissant and the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) for Agentic AI.

speakers.name: Tianyi Han
speakers.bio: Tianyi Han is an Architect Solution focused on AI systems, agent governance, and decision-support tooling. His work explores how to make AI-driven systems more controllable, auditable, and reproducible through runtime policy enforcement, traceability, and replay. He is currently building systems that bridge the gap between experimental LLM applications and production-grade AI infrastructure, with a focus on governance, observability, and reliable execution.

speakers.name: Dr Hai-Xu Cheng
speakers.bio: Dr Hai-Xu Cheng currently works as the CTO of Rothwell International after retiring from the role of IBM Global Lead and IBM GCG CTO of standards and open source. His current major focus is providing consulting services for enterprise clients at C-level on architectures, standards, and open source. In his prior role at IBM, he led the global and China teams working to develop open-source communities and technologies spanning AI, data and analytics, cloud computing, quantum computing, and blockchain, advocating for clients to adopt open technologies to fuel innovation in both technical and business domains.

speakers.name: Joanna Kramer
speakers.bio: Currently based in Paris, Joanna's career has blended industry and research. After earning her MSc from University of Oxford's Internet Institute, where she studied the breakdown of digital platforms and the creation of digital 'ruins,' she co-founded WISE with Michelle Nie and Nitya Kuthiala to build community and foster connections among women working across AI safety, ethics, and governance. One year later, the network has expanded to 5 WISE chapters across Brussels, Delhi, London, Paris, and Washington, D.C. In addition, Joanna leads market research and technical marketing initiatives at an applied AI research lab.
